the energy of the primary charge separation in the reaction centre is dissipated via recombination in a majority of the oxidized RCs.

we report on an ultrafast charge recombining process in oxidizing reaction centres of Rhodobacter sphearoides that is not present in fully reduced reaction centres.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the fundamental processes that underpin the conversion of light energy to chemical energy in the reaction centres of purple bacteria, and the mechanisms that prevent the production of potentially damaging excited electronic states in these systems.
the molecular mechanism of the photoprotective process that operates under mildly oxidizing redox conditions in the reaction centre of Rhodobacter (Rba.) sphaeroidesis.
understanding the molecular basis of the intrinsic photoprotection that operates under fluctuating conditions in photosynthetic reaction centres (RC) of purple bacteria.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the RCs in the partially oxidized state are more efficient in dissipating the excitation energy than in the fully reduced state.
the energy dissipation process observed here is a photoprotective mechanism that prevents the formation of potentially harmful excited states in the presence of oxidizing conditions.
the RC is a very complex and dynamic system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have discovered a new mechanism to protect photosynthetic reaction centers from damage by light and oxygen.
we show that the energy dissipation mechanism is not a single mechanism, but a single mechanism is not a simple mechanism.
the RCs are not only the primary energy converter, but also a primary photoprotective device.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the energy dissipation process is not just a mechanism to protect the RC from triplet state photodamage, but is also an effective way to dissipate energy from an excited RC in the presence of a mildly oxidizing environment.
there are two different pathways for energy transfer in the RC.
we have shown how the energy of a single photon absorbed by a photosynthetic reaction centre can be safely dissipated in a single, ultrafast step.
